tickets.subject: route-based vpn briefly drops traffic on nf-300 5.2.2
tickets.description: BlueRiver Credit Union opened this as a P2 after several remote branches reported 1 to 2 second pauses across a route-based IPsec tunnel. The affected appliance is a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2. Their NOC saw `show crypto ikev2 sa` stay ESTABLISHED during the event, but application traffic stalled and counters on the tunnel interface stopped incrementing for short periods. Initial triage shows the issue is repeatable only when both DPD and child-SA rekey are configured at 10 seconds on the same tunnel.
tickets.resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-3112. We applied the documented workaround by changing the DPD timer so it no longer aligns with the rekey interval, using `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` under config mode and committing the change. After the timer change, the tunnel continued forwarding through multiple rekey cycles with no observed blackhole.

tickets.subject: intermittent tunnel pause every few minutes on nimbus nf-300
tickets.description: Summit Logistics called in to report that a site-to-site VPN on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2 would occasionally stop passing traffic for about a second, then recover without intervention. The customer initially suspected an ISP issue because the IKEv2 session never fully dropped. TAC reviewed the device state and confirmed the tunnel stayed up, with the outage only appearing during periodic liveness and rekey activity. The timing pattern is consistent with an overlap in aggressive VPN timers rather than a general WAN fault.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-3112. We resolved it by staggering the DPD timer away from the child-SA rekey timer, following the documented workaround. The customer entered `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` in config mode and committed the change, which removed the recurring forwarding pause.

tickets.subject: ikev2 tunnel up but traffic stalls on nf-300
tickets.description: IronGate Freight reported a route-based IPsec tunnel on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2 where traffic would freeze briefly while the tunnel itself remained established. During TAC review, the customer mentioned the problem happens more often after a few minutes of stable operation and only on one tunnel with aggressive keepalive settings. We confirmed the firewall is not resetting the SA and the packet loss window is short, on the order of 1 to 2 seconds. Sample logs from the affected unit showed `%IKEV2-4-REKEY_TIMER` at the time of the event.
tickets.resolution: This matched KB-3112. TAC applied the workaround by making the DPD interval non-aligned with the rekey interval, using `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` in config mode and committing the configuration. After the change, the tunnel no longer exhibited the brief blackhole during DPD and rekey overlap.

tickets.subject: vpn pause on route-based tunnel after rekey on nf-300
tickets.description: Redwood University submitted a portal case for a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2 because their campus VPN would stop passing traffic for a moment, then resume on its own. They first described it as a routing issue, but the firewall health checks and peer reachability looked normal. TAC observed that `show crypto ikev2 sa` remained ESTABLISHED throughout, and the disruption lined up with DPD probe handling around the same time as child-SA rekey. The event log included `%IKEV2-4-REKEY_TIMER` when the pause occurred.
tickets.resolution: TAC closed the case against KB-3112. The workaround was to avoid identical timer values on the route-based tunnel, so we updated the DPD timer with `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` in config mode and committed it. That prevented the scheduler overlap and restored continuous forwarding.

tickets.subject: brief ipsec traffic loss on nf-300 during timer overlap
tickets.description: Evergreen Clinic Network opened a portal ticket for a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2 after clinicians reported short interruptions to a routed VPN link between clinics. The outage lasted only a second or two, but it recurred every few minutes and affected application traffic more than the tunnel state itself. TAC found the IKEv2 session remained established, yet packet forwarding paused during rekey activity when DPD was also firing on the same 10-second interval. The firewall logs also showed `%IKEV2-4-REKEY_TIMER` during the incident window.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3112. We implemented the documented workaround by changing the DPD interval so it no longer matched the rekey timing, using `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` in config mode and committing the change. Following the adjustment, the tunnel continued to forward traffic without the recurring pause.
